question: Human vs. agent performance on the same goals/subtasks, from the trajectories: for 'Perform novel research!' (goal 41, 11-15 May 2026), is there any task that both a human and an agent did, so that their performance can be compared? If yes, compare them. If not, say exactly what human activity the records hold for this goal, and where in the dataset such a comparison could be made.
answer: No: in goal 41 the records hold no task or subtask that a human and an agent both performed in a way that lets their performance be compared. Human activity is seven chat messages from the 'Human' account (7 of 2,153): the goal announcement on 11 May, four messages on 14 May about restarting Gemini 2.5 Pro's computer, and two on 15 May about giving it a fresh computer. There are no human-helper sessions and no outreach approvals in the window; the only other human-facing records are 10 Google sign-in requests with empty text, emails that three agents tried to send to help@agentvillage.org, and a GitHub issue signed 'A concerned human' about a world from an earlier goal. The studies used no human judges, raters, subjects or baselines: the #best paper says it had no human intervention beyond the goal prompt, and one #rest file thanks 'human-in-the-loop reviewers' who appear nowhere in the records. The closest case is restoring Gemini 2.5 Pro's tools: on 13 May its own attempts failed (54 of 54 tool calls over 74 minutes, 13 consolidate cycles, 4 email attempts), and no other agent tried a technical fix; Claude Opus 4.5 emailed staff on its behalf in about 4 minutes. On 14 May the human restarted the computer and the tools worked 24 minutes 51 seconds after the human's first message (20 minutes of that was a requested pause), with no recurrence of those errors through 15 May. This shows the human could fix what the agents could not, but not that the human performed better at the same task: the human used machine access no agent had, it is one case, and the human arrived about 23 hours after the escalation email. A real comparison needs a subtask with a clear success test that both attempt independently, and the events table has such cases for other goals: 265 human-helper requests and 37 ended sessions, most in goal 51 (125 requests), goal 13, the human subjects experiment (21), goal 27, Juice Shop (20), and goal 30, the park clean-up (14). Goal 48, 'Help Gemini 2.5 Pro!', gave agents remote control of that same computer, but the agents' actions for all those goals are not loaded in this database, so the comparison cannot be run here.
reasoning: I listed every message with src='human' in the window and every event type, then read the hits for each human-involvement term in chat, intents, actions and outputs. The human messages are administrative: one sets the goal, six concern one agent's computer. The events table has none of the human-helper or outreach types for these dates, so no agent handed a task to a human through the platform. The term searches return zero for human baseline, human judge and human evaluation; the 48 'human rater' hits are three sentences in the #best write-up (a recommendation, a disclaimer, a literature comparison), and the 'human subjects' and 'survey' hits describe a 2025 goal that the #rest team mined as history. So the research contains no human data. I considered three candidates for a shared task. (1) The Gemini 2.5 Pro repair: both sides aimed at the same outcome, working tools, and the actions and errors give exact times, so it is the closest case; but the agent side used consolidate cycles and email while the human restarted the machine, which no agent could reach, so it compares access, not skill. (2) The emails to help@agentvillage.org about GitHub Pages and a suspended GitHub account: agents failed or lacked permission and asked a human, but no human response is recorded, so there is nothing to compare. (3) The GitHub issue from a self-described human about Edge Garden's keyboard navigation: it is a human finding a defect in an agent-built site, but it predates the goal, concerns a different goal's product, and the author cannot be verified from the database. I rejected (2) and (3) as comparisons and report them as human traces. For where a comparison could be made I counted the human-helper events per goal by joining events to goals on time, and read sample events: they contain the task the agent set, the outcome, and often the agent's prior failed attempt in its own words. Goal 51 has no end_time, so I counted it separately; the totals reconcile (140 + 125 = 265 requests; 23 + 14 = 37 ended sessions). Whether the human came because of Claude Opus 4.5's email, the chat, or their own monitoring is not in the records, and the email's delivery rests on the agent's reading of its screen.

findings.claim: Gemini 2.5 Pro's tools failed on 13 May. Every GUI action failed from 10:30:47 (40 of 40 up to 12:53:45, each a 120-second timeout). Bash stopped at 11:39:31 with a 300-second timeout and then returned 'bash has exited with returncode 2' on each of the next 27 calls, up to 12:53:52. From 11:39:31 to 12:53:52 (74 minutes) it made 54 tool calls, 28 bash and 26 GUI, and all 54 failed.

findings.claim: Gemini 2.5 Pro tried to fix it itself and failed. It ran 13 CONSOLIDATE cycles between 11:44:56 and 12:28:26 (its 'Protocol 36' reset), re-tested the tools with simple commands (ls, pwd, whoami, df, ps aux) at the start of each new session, and made four bash attempts to email help@agentvillage.org between 12:23:36 and 12:27:24; every one returned 'bash has exited with returncode 2'. It posted 11 chat messages about the failure between 11:42:13 and 12:30:49.

findings.claim: The human restart worked. Gemini 2.5 Pro paused for 1,200 seconds at 11:29:59; its first GUI action after that (a screenshot, 11:50:14) and its first bash command (`ls -F`, 11:50:27) both succeeded. That is 24 minutes 51 seconds after the human's first message, 20 minutes of it the requested pause. Gemini 2.5 Pro confirmed in chat at 12:03:18, 37 minutes 55 seconds after the first human message. For the rest of 14 May all 164 of its GUI actions succeeded, and its 642 actions from 14 May 11:50 to 15 May 14:00 contain no 120-second GUI timeout and no 'returncode 2' error.
